arxiv-1706-01477.title: Heat content and horizontal mean curvature on the Heisenberg group
arxiv-1706-01477.creator: Jeremy Tyson Jing Wang
arxiv-1706-01477.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Jeremy Tyson Jing Wang. We identify the short time asymptotics of the sub-Riemannian heat content for a smoothly bounded domain in the first Heisenberg group. Our asymptotic formula generalizes prior work by van den Berg–Le Gall and van den Berg–Gilkey to the sub-Riemannian context, and identifies the first few coefficients in the sub-Riemannian heat content in terms of the horizontal perimeter and the total horizontal mean curvature of the boundary.

arxiv-1806-04958.title: Lehmann-Suwa Residues of codimension one holomorphic foliations and applications
arxiv-1806-04958.creator: Arturo Fernández-Pérez, Jimmy Támara
arxiv-1806-04958.description: Abstract . Let ℱ \mathscr{F} be a singular codimension one holomorphic foliation on a compact complex manifold X X of dimension at least three such that its singular set has codimension at least two. In this paper, we determine Lehmann-Suwa residues of ℱ \mathscr{F} as multiples of complex numbers by integration currents along irreducible complex subvarieties of X X .

arxiv-1911-02782.title: S2ORC: The Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus
arxiv-1911-02782.creator: Kyle Lo, Lucy Lu Wang, Mark Neumann, Rodney Kinney, Daniel S. Weld
arxiv-1911-02782.description: Abstract We introduce S2ORC , 1 1 1 Instructions for access to the data and model are available at https://github.com/allenai/s2orc/ . a large corpus of 81.1M English-language academic papers spanning many academic disciplines. The corpus consists of rich metadata, paper abstracts, resolved bibliographic references, as well as structured full text for 8.1M open access papers.

arxiv-2206-05385.title: Ring Seismology of the Ice Giants Uranus and Neptune
arxiv-2206-05385.creator: Joseph A. A’Hearn, Matthew M. Hedman, Christopher R. Mankovich, Hima Aramona, Mark S. Marley
arxiv-2206-05385.description: Abstract We assess the prospect of using ring seismology to probe the interiors of the ice giants Uranus and Neptune. We do this by calculating normal mode spectra for different interior models of Uranus and Neptune using the stellar oscillation code GYRE .

arxiv-2301-06993.title: Your Day in Your Pocket: Complex Activity Recognition from Smartphone Accelerometers
arxiv-2301-06993.creator: Emma Bouton–Bessac, Lakmal Meegahapola, Daniel Gatica-Perez
arxiv-2301-06993.description: Abstract Human Activity Recognition (HAR) enables context-aware user experiences where mobile apps can alter content and interactions depending on user activities. Hence, smartphones have become valuable for HAR as they allow large, and diversified data collection. Although previous work in HAR managed to detect simple activities (i.e., sitting, walking, running) with good accuracy using inertial sensors (i.e.

arxiv-2302-04237.title: Black Box Adversarial Prompting for Foundation Models
arxiv-2302-04237.creator: Natalie Maus, Patrick Chao, Eric Wong, Jacob Gardner
arxiv-2302-04237.description: Abstract Prompting interfaces allow users to quickly adjust the output of generative models in both vision and language. However, small changes and design choices in the prompt can lead to significant differences in the output. In this work, we develop a black-box framework for generating adversarial prompts for unstructured image and text generation.

arxiv-2307-01244.title: TR-ARPES Signal in Pumped Semiconductors within Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach (DPOA)
arxiv-2307-01244.creator: Amir Eskandari-asl 1 and Adolfo Avella 1,2,3
arxiv-2307-01244.description: Abstract In this manuscript, after discussing in detail the internals of our recently developed method, the dynamical projective operatorial approach (DPOA), we provide the framework to apply this method to pumped semiconductor lattice systems and, in particular, to study and analyze their electronic excitations and TR-ARPES signal.

arxiv-2308-04253.title: Existence of strong solutions for a perfect elastic beam interacting with Navier-Stokes equations
arxiv-2308-04253.creator: Sebastian Schwarzacher 1,2, Pei Su 1
arxiv-2308-04253.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Schwarzacher 1,2, Pei Su 1. A perfectly elastic beam is situated on top of a two dimensional fluid canister. The beam is deforming in accordance to an interaction with a Navier-Stokes fluid. Hence a hyperbolic equation is coupled to the Navier-Stokes equation. The coupling is partially of geometric nature, as the geometry of the fluid domain is changing in accordance to the motion of the beam.

arxiv-2401-06477.title: Kun: Answer Polishment for Chinese Self-Alignment with Instruction Back-Translation
arxiv-2401-06477.creator: [0.5mm] Xingwei Qu, Jiawei Guo, Xinrun Du, Qi Jia, [0.5mm] Chenghua Lin, Wenhao Huang, Jie Fu, Ge Zhang, [2mm] 01.AI, University of Waterloo, HKUST
arxiv-2401-06477.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce Kun 1 1 1 The dataset is named Kun as Chinese pronunciation of Humpback Li et al. 2023c . , a novel approach for creating high-quality instruction-tuning datasets for large language models (LLMs) without relying on manual annotations.

arxiv-2404-00108.title: Efficient Data-Free Model Stealing with Label Diversity
arxiv-2404-00108.creator: Yiyong Liu, Rui Wen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
arxiv-2404-00108.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yiyong Liu, Rui Wen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang. Machine learning as a Service (MLaaS) allows users to query the machine learning model in an API manner, which provides an opportunity for users to enjoy the benefits brought by the high-performance model trained on valuable data. This interface boosts the proliferation of machine learning based applications, while on the other hand, it introduces the attack surface for model stealing attacks.

arxiv-2406-05794.title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
arxiv-2406-05794.creator: Kiseung Kim Jay-Yoon Lee
arxiv-2406-05794.description: Abstract The Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework utilizes a combination of parametric knowledge and external knowledge to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on open-domain question answering tasks. However, the RAG framework suffers from performance degradation when the query is accompanied by irrelevant contexts.

arxiv-2410-14155.title: Towards Faithful Natural Language Explanations: A Study Using Activation Patching in Large Language Models
arxiv-2410-14155.creator: Wei Jie Yeo, Ranjan Satapathy, Erik Cambria
arxiv-2410-14155.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are capable of generating persuasive Natural Language Explanations (NLEs) to justify their answers. However, the faithfulness of these explanations should not be readily trusted at face value. Recent studies have proposed various methods to measure the faithfulness of NLEs, typically by inserting perturbations at the explanation or feature level.

arxiv-2410-15127.title: Verification and Interpretation-Driven Safe Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework
arxiv-2410-15127.creator: Zixuan Yang, Jiaqi Zheng, Guihai Chen
arxiv-2410-15127.description: Abstract Ensuring verifiable and interpretable safety of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is crucial for its deployment in real-world applications. Existing approaches like verification-in-the-loop training, however, face challenges such as difficulty in deployment, inefficient training, lack of interpretability, and suboptimal performance in property satisfaction and reward performance.

arxiv-2411-07235.title: Circulating Currents in Electric Machines: Positive Impact of The End Windings Length on Losses
arxiv-2411-07235.creator: Taha El Hajji, Antti Lehikoinen, Anouar Belahcen
arxiv-2411-07235.description: Abstract Circulating currents occurring in windings of electric machines received rising interest recent years. Circulating currents represent unwanted currents flowing between parallel-connected conductors. This phenomenon is due to various reasons such as asymmetries in the winding and differences in electric potential between parallel-connected conductors.

arxiv-2503-18617.title: Scaling Laws for Emulation of Stellar Spectra
arxiv-2503-18617.creator: Tomasz Różański 1, Yuan-Sen Ting (丁源森)
arxiv-2503-18617.description: Abstract Neural network-based emulators for the inference of stellar parameters and elemental abundances represent an increasingly popular methodology in modern spectroscopic surveys. However, these approaches are often constrained by their emulation precision and domain transfer capabilities. Greater generalizability has previously been achieved only with significantly larger model architectures, as demonstrated by Transformer-based models in natural language processing.

arxiv-2510-11207.title: Fibration Symmetries and Cluster Synchronization in Multi-Body Systems
arxiv-2510-11207.creator: Margherita Bertè, Tommaso Gili
arxiv-2510-11207.description: Abstract Based on recent advances in fibration symmetry theory, we investigate how structural symmetries influence synchronization in systems with higher-order interactions (HOI). Using bipartite graph representations, we identify a node partition in fibres, based on equivalent incidence relations in hypergraphs.

pmc-10520358.creator: Sang-Yun Lee, Hyun Ju Hwang, You Jin Song, Dayoung Lee, Bosung Ku, Jason K. Sa, Dong Woo Lee
pmc-10520358.description: A pillar dishe for subculture of 3D cultured cells on hydrogel spots (Matrigel and alginate) have been developed. pmc-10742671.title: Designing a Novel Approach Using a Greedy and Information-Theoretic Clustering-Based Algorithm for Anonymizing Microdata Sets
pmc-10742671.creator: Reza Ahmadi Khatir, Habib Izadkhah, Jafar Razmara, Shu-Chuan Chu
pmc-10742671.description: Data anonymization is a technique that safeguards individuals’ privacy by modifying attribute values in published data. However, increased modifications enhance privacy but diminish the utility of published data, necessitating a balance between privacy and utility levels. K-Anonymity is a crucial anonymization technique that generates k-anonymous clusters, where the probability of disclosing a record is 1/k.

In the present study, we investigate the change in occupational risk during the subsequent pandemic phases and we propose an estimate of the incidence of the cases by economic sector, based on the analysis of insurance claims for compensation for Covid-19.MethodsCovid-19 epidemiological data available for the general population and injury claims of workers covered by

pmc-11462758.title: Redefining chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) regulation: China’s responses to address secondary cancer risks of CAR-T therapy
pmc-11462758.creator: Ruirong Tan, Rui Li, Meng-Yuan Dai, Miao Liu, Junning Zhao
pmc-11462758.description: Since the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy in 2017, it has marked a major breakthrough in cancer treatment, leading to a surge in global research and applications in this field.

pmc-12445039.title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis uncovers novel genetic variants associated with olfactory dysfunction
pmc-12445039.creator: Mohammed Aslam Imtiaz, Konstantinos Melas, Adrienne Tin, Valentina Talevi, Honglei Chen, Myriam Fornage, Srishti Shrestha, Martin Gögele, David Emmert, Cristian Pattaro, Peter Pramstaller, Franz Förster, Katrin Horn, Thomas H. Mosley, Christian Fuchsberger, Markus Scholz, Monique M.B. Breteler, N. A
pmc-12445039.description: BackgroundOlfactory dysfunction is among the earliest signs of many age-related neurodegenerative diseases and has been associated with increased mortality in older adults; however, its genetic basis remains largely unknown. Therefore, here we aimed to elucidate its genetic architecture through a genome-wide association study meta-analysis (GWMA).

pmc-12448025.title: Improving fermentation quality of Sichuan radish paocai through co-inoculation of homo- and heterofermentative lactic acid bacteria
pmc-12448025.creator: Yiwen Fan, Quanyou Guo
pmc-12448025.description: This study investigates the effects of lactic acid bacteria, including Lactobacillus brevis (B), Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (P), and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus (R), on the fermentation and quality of Sichuan radish paocai (SRP) through both single and mixed inoculations. The mixed culture PRB (P + R + B) achieved rapid acidification and balanced homo-heterofermentative metabolism.

pmc-12815812.title: Toward the future management of patients with CML and Ph + ALL: real-world safety insights from dasatinib pharmacovigilance
pmc-12815812.creator: Zhen Lu, Guangbin Shang, Yingjian Zeng, Xiaonan Lu
pmc-12815812.description: BackgroundDasatinib, a second-generation BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has transformed treatment for chronic myeloid leukemia and Philadelphia chromosome–positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia. However, its broad kinase inhibition leads to distinct adverse events (AEs), requiring systematic post-marketing surveillance.ObjectiveTo evaluate dasatinib-associated AEs using the United States Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and identify potential safety signals.

pmc-13266149.title: Anti-inflammatory effect of Canis familiaris (dog) gingival derived microorganisms on Porphyromonas gingivalis derived lipopolysaccharide treated RAW 264.7 macrophage
pmc-13266149.creator: Jeong-Woong Park, Seon-Ae Choi, Jeong Won Kim, Jung-Hwan Ji, Kong-Min Kim, Jun-Kyung Park, Gui Hwan Han, Seonghun Im
pmc-13266149.description: Porphyromonas gingivalis is recognized for its significant association with periodontal diseases, encompassing conditions like gingivitis and periodontitis. P. gingivalis infiltrates periodontal tissues, liberating diverse outer membrane vesicles, notably lipopolysaccharide (LPS). These vesicles serve as triggers for innate immune responses, fostering inflammation.

pmc-13535104.creator: Wayne Yunpeng Fu, Allan C. Spradling
pmc-13535104.description: Ovarian follicles in most species are assumed to develop using a single pathway. However, in Drosophila pupae, lineage tracing 2937 single-cell clones identified three follicle ‘waves’ that follow distinct programs arrayed anterior to posterior in the germarium and developing ovarioles. 40 primordial germ cells (PGCs) become anterior germline stem cells that produce ‘wave 2’ follicles throughout adulthood.
